Subject: Intro: Skyhook x Redwood partnership opportunity (rev-share + lead crediting)

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week — excited by the overlap between Skyhook's observability connectors and Redwood's inference platform. We put together a short one-pager that outlines a potential commercial approach (attached).

High-level asks from our side:
- A simple revenue-share for software usage tied to customers we joint-win (we typically start pilots at ~15–20% first year).
- Clear lead registration / intro crediting so reps know which deals to credit to Skyhook (we prefer a 60-day claim window but are flexible).
- A lightweight pilot agreement to start with 10 enterprise customers for a 3-month technical validation.

Would you and your partnerships/commercial ops folks be open to a short call next week to run through model and sample contract language? If useful, I can include our legal lead on the thread — they have an initial redline ready.

Hi team — forwarding Lena's note and one-pager. Quick summary of asks: rev-share, lead registration window, and a 3-month pilot (10 customers). Lena suggested 15–20% for year-1.

My initial thinking for a pilot-friendly commercial:
- Pilot revenue-share: 18% of Redwood-recognized gross for any joint-won customers during pilot term (12-week pilot).
- Post-pilot standard: 12% on renewals / year-2+ (reduce once product integration is GA).
- Lead registration: 45-day claim window from Skyhook's first documented intro; require HubSpot form + dedicated MAP (mutual action plan) to lock the intro.
- Demo/POC credits: offer up to $X in free hosted credits (we can table $ amount) for joint customers during pilot.

Can legal or commercial ops propose redlines to a short pilot MSA? Ben / Karthik — any immediate concerns on the percentages or the 45-day intro window? Camila — will you want to own partner enablement / co-marketing for this?

I cc'd Lena so she sees our starting posture. Planning a 30 min sync next Tue?

Thanks,
Monica Patel

Monica — thanks for the summary. Curious about two operational items before we lock percentages:
1) Lead hygiene / proof: we should require a timestamped HubSpot contact + a one-line note from Skyhook rep (email thread PDF acceptable) to validate an intro. That reduces disputes.
2) Demo credit abuse: recommend we cap credits per account for pilot (e.g., $2,500 credits / account) and a total pilot pool cap.

If we go 18% pilot / 12% post-pilot that feels OK for a limited cohort (10 accounts). For larger co-sell scale we should step down the rev-share and replace with MDF or co-sell credits.

I'll run a quick commercial draft and drop redlines to the attached doc (ask legal for the MSA template).

-b

Subject: Skyhook draft (redline) and questions on lead capture

Hi Monica / Ben / team,

Attached is a redline (Skyhook_Redline_v1.docx) of a short pilot SOW + rev-share schedule. Two commercial points we flagged:
- Skyhook asks for a 60-day lead registration window (we prefer this for enterprise cycles).
- Revenue-share waterfall: Skyhook proposed 20% total for year-1 net-recognized revenue, with a 5% step-down after year-2 conditioned on renewal coverage.

Operational question: what exact lead fields do you need to validate an intro? We want to avoid unnecessary friction; happy to have the HubSpot contact + email thread as minimum but would like the ability to retroactively validate introductions up to 90 days if the account converts slowly.

Also proposed: a joint MAP in Drive to track the 10 pilot customers, milestones, and POC owners. We included comments in the redline about reporting cadence and invoicing frequency (quarterly).

Attaching: Skyhook_Redline_v1.docx

Thanks,
Skyhook Analytics Legal (on behalf of Lena Park)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2028 09:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Skyhook draft (redline) and questions on lead capture — proposed pilot MAP and next steps

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks, appreciate the speed. Quick consolidation from our side and proposed next steps so we can get a DocuSignable SOW live this week: 

Commercial (pilot):
- Pilot term: 12 weeks, up to 10 joint customers
- Pilot rev-share: 18% of Redwood-recognized revenue attributable to Skyhook-sourced customers during pilot term
- Post-pilot default: 12% on renewals / standard commercial (we can revisit after pilot results)

Lead registration / validation:
- Registration window: 45 days from first documented intro (HubSpot contact + initial email thread).
- Retroactive validation: allow retroactive claims up to 90 days if Skyhook supplies the email thread and a documented sequence showing engagement, but disputes after 90 days are closed.
- Claim process: Skyhook files registration in HubSpot (specific form), we assign a registration ID, and the MAP (link below) confirms sales owners.

Operational items:
- Demo/POC credits: pilot pool capped at $2,500 / account and $20k total across pilot cohort.
- Reporting / invoicing: quarterly invoicing; Redwood provides monthly join-customer usage snapshot for invoicing reconciliation.

Next steps:
1) Ben / legal: I'll upload a short SOW that reflects the items above and include Skyhook redline comments.
2) Lena / Skyhook legal: confirm acceptance of 45-day window + 90-day retroactive validation (we propose this split as a middle ground).
3) Camila: can you draft the MAP spreadsheet and co-marketing checklist? I attached a starter MAP for your edit.

Attaching: MAP_Skyhook_Pilot.xlsx

Link to MAP: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSkyhookPilot
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DEAL-98765

If we can get yes on the 45/90 compromise today, we can cut a pilot SOW and execute by Wed. Lena — are you able to confirm?

Cheers,
